question: Should OpenClaw add a broader config mode that disables URL tokens, HTTPS requirements, device identity, pairing, or tailnet trust checks for private deployments?
rationale: The request changes operator-auth and transport security boundaries; current source and docs expose narrower tokenless paths but intentionally do not provide the full bypass requested here.

options.title: Keep current boundaries
options.body: Treat current token/password, trusted-proxy, verified Tailscale Serve, and explicit break-glass paths as the supported surface and reject broader blanket bypasses.

options.title: Sponsor a narrower dangerous mode
options.body: Design a named private-ingress or tailnet policy with warnings, docs, startup checks, and tests instead of a generic `urlToken=0/1` switch.

options.title: Accept broad external-trust bypass
options.body: Allow self-managed deployments to disable multiple Gateway safeguards and rely on external network controls for operator access.

recommendation.title: Keep current boundaries
recommendation.body: Treat current token/password, trusted-proxy, verified Tailscale Serve, and explicit break-glass paths as the supported surface and reject broader blanket bypasses.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is tied to the most recent Gateway auth hardening and the merged Tailscale no-auth rejection that defines the current boundary.
